Class WhoSecurity

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.spring.security.WhoSecurity
public final class WhoSecurity extends Object
Entry point for mounting who into a Spring Security chain the application writes itself. 
@Bean
SecurityFilterChain chain(HttpSecurity http, WhoPublicPaths publicPaths) {
  http.with(WhoSecurity.all(), Customizer.withDefaults())
      .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
          .requestMatchers(publicPaths.patterns()).permitAll()
          .anyRequest().authenticated());
  return http.build();
}

Without a chain of the application's own, who's autoconfiguration registers exactly this chain. For finer control, mount methods one at a time with WhoWebSecurity.passwordless() or a module's own configurer.

    • stateless

      public static WhoStatelessConfigurer stateless()
      Returns a configurer that mounts only who's stateless sign-in methods (API keys, bearer JWTs) into a chain with no session and no CSRF, answering a signed-out request with 401. It gives an API a chain of its own beside a browser chain: 
      @Bean @Order(1)
SecurityFilterChain api(HttpSecurity http) {
  http.securityMatcher("/api/**")
      .with(WhoSecurity.stateless(), Customizer.withDefaults())
      .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a.anyRequest().authenticated());
  return http.build();
}

@Bean @Order(2)
SecurityFilterChain web(HttpSecurity http, WhoPublicPaths publicPaths) {
  http.with(WhoWebSecurity.passwordless(), Customizer.withDefaults())
      .authorizeHttpRequests(a -> a
          .requestMatchers(publicPaths.patterns()).permitAll()
          .anyRequest().authenticated());
  return http.build();
}

      A browser's session cookie signs nothing in on the API chain.
